data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English 'beald-hygel' meaning 'bald' and 'hygel' meaning 'higher'. The name Balliol is of Old English origin and means 'House of God'. It was originally used as a surname for someone who lived near or owned a church or monastery. The name Balliol carries the meaning “House of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Balliol usually hope their child will grow to embody house of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Balliol
in_latin.long_meaning: The surname Balliol is of French origin, derived from the Old French 'de Balliol', which refers to a place name in Normandy. The name itself may be related to the Latin 'ballium', meaning 'bravery' or 'courage'. In early Christian tradition, courage and bravery were highly valued virtues.

in_english.long_meaning: The name Balliol originates from a place name in Normandy, France. It is associated with the Latin 'ballium', signifying bravery or courage. Historically, the name Balliol has been linked to several notable figures, including John Balliol, a 13th-century King of Scots. The name symbolizes strength and valor, reflecting key Christian virtues.
